name: John H. Peck
tagline: Top rated Personal Injury attorney in Boston, Massachusetts
side_practice_areas: Personal Injury, Medical Malpractice, Employment & Labor
about: As the president and trial attorney at Peck Trial Attorneys, PC, located in Boston, Massachusetts, John H. Peck offers strategic legal representation to individuals and families in complex personal injury and employment law matters. His practice focuses on advocating for plaintiffs in cases involving motor vehicle accidents, trucking accidents, premises liability, construction accidents, medical malpractice, birth injuries, brain injuries, animal bites and wrongful death claims. He also represents employees in wrongful termination and other employment law disputes.

Known for his results-driven and client-centered approach, Mr. Peck works closely with clients facing life-altering injuries and difficult legal challenges. He is committed to pursuing accountability on behalf of injured individuals while seeking favorable outcomes through strategic negotiation and litigation. His experience handling catastrophic injury claims allows him to navigate complicated medical, financial and liability issues on behalf of his clients.

Mr. Peck has built a reputation for handling high-stakes matters involving catastrophic injuries and complex liability issues. Whether representing victims of serious accidents or employees facing workplace injustices, he strives to deliver practical legal guidance tailored to each client’s unique circumstances.

Among his notable matters, Mr. Peck and his team represented a young man who suffered catastrophic injuries after being struck by a vehicle while crossing the street. The driver fled the scene following the collision, prompting an extensive investigation. Through persistent advocacy and investigative efforts, he and his team secured more than $1 million for the young man and his family.

Mr. Peck earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Hobart and William Smith Colleges in 2011. He later obtained his Juris Doctor from Suffolk University Law School in 2014. In that same year, he was admitted to practice law in Massachusetts.
